title: Enroll a Program
description: How a Program Admin enrolls a Linux Foundation project's mentorship program, and what each step of the form asks for.
content: Program Admins enroll a program for a Linux Foundation project and bring on paid, mentored contributors for a multi-week term. LFX runs applications, stipends, evaluations and compliance; the project scopes the work and reviews it. Before you begin You must be signed in to LFX as a Program Admin for the project. Scope the work for a single term. Name at least two mentors. Confirm funding before enrolling — an unfunded program cannot open. What the form asks for Enrollment is a three-step form in the LFX Admin area. Gather these before you start; you can save a draft and come back. Step | What it asks for | ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 1. Program Details | Program name, program description, Code of Conduct URL, the Linux Foundation project, repository and website URLs, program logo, technologies, CII Best Practices project ID. You can import details from a program you have run before. | 2. Program Setup | Required and desirable skills, custom term dates, non-technical interest areas, program terms. Mentors are invited later, once the program is approved. | 3. Prerequisites | What candidates must complete to qualify: resume, participation permission, terms and conditions, cover letter topics, coding challenge, school enrollment verification, and any custom prerequisites. Plus the platform terms. | Steps 1. Select Enroll a Program from the top navigation. This opens the Admin area of LFX at app.lfx.dev/mentorship/admin. 2. Sign in as a Program Admin. 3. Complete Program Details, Program Setup and Prerequisites. 4. Submit the enrollment. After you submit 1. The LFX Mentorship team reviews your enrollment, usually within 2 business days. A program that is not approved is rejected. 2. Once approved, invite mentors from the Mentors tab. 3. The program opens for applications, and applicants appear in your workspace. Why offer a program Grow your contributor base — most graduated mentees keep contributing after the term, often becoming reviewers and core contributors. Move work you keep deferring — tooling, tests, docs and instrumentation suit a scoped term well. Funding you control — where a program is funded, the stipend comes from project funds, a foundation pool or a direct sponsor. Program administration handled — LFX runs applications, eligibility checks, stipend payments, evaluations and compliance. A wider pool of candidates — your program is listed alongside every other LFX program. A record you can point to — every term keeps its mentees, approved work and outcomes. Related sections Mentor Invitations — what the mentors you invite will see Program Pages — how your program will look once it is live Getting Started

title: Getting Started
description: What LFX Mentorship is, who it is for, and what you need before you take part.
content: LFX Mentorship pairs contributors with experienced members of open source projects. Over a multi-week term you take on real, scoped work from the project's backlog and review it with a named mentor. Who takes part Role | What they do | Where they work | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | Mentee | Applies to a program, completes scoped tasks across the term, and takes a final evaluation | app.lfx.dev/mentorship/mentee | Mentor | Scopes the work, reviews what a mentee submits, and scores applicants | app.lfx.dev/mentorship/mentor | Program Admin | Enrolls a project's program, invites mentors, and runs the term | app.lfx.dev/mentorship/admin | Browsing programs, mentees and mentors on this site needs no account. Applying, mentoring or administering a program all happen in LFX and need an LF ID. How a term works 1. Build your profile — add your skills, links and a short introduction. Mentors read this first. 2. Apply to programs — up to three applications at a time. Each is reviewed by the program's mentors. 3. Get matched — mentors score applicants on skills fit and intent, then accept for the term. 4. Do the work — scoped tasks with regular reviews from your mentor. 5. Graduate — pass the final evaluation and receive your stipend installments, where the program is funded. Who can apply You are 18 or older. You can commit consistent hours for the full term. You may have up to 3 applications open at a time. You may only complete one LFX Mentorship program in your career. Not every program is funded. Where a stipend is offered, the amount varies by program and by your country of residence, and the program page states it before you apply. Key terms Program — a project's mentorship offering. A program belongs to one Linux Foundation project and lists the skills it is looking for. Term — the dated run of a program. A program can run several terms over the years; each has its own dates and its own mentees. Application — a mentee's or mentor's request to join a program for a term. An application that is turned down is declined. Program status — where a program sits in moderation. A program that is not approved is rejected; that word is never used for an application. Prerequisite — something a candidate must supply before an application counts as complete, such as a resume, a cover letter or a coding challenge. Stipend — the payment some programs make to a mentee in milestone installments. Related sections Programs — find and read a program before you apply Mentees — become a mentee and apply to a program Mentors — become a mentor or respond to an invitation Enroll a Program — offer a program for your project Getting Started FAQ

title: Getting Started FAQ
description: Common questions about eligibility, stipends, time commitment and applying to LFX Mentorship.
content: Is there a stipend? Not every program is funded. Where a stipend is offered it varies by program and by your country of residence, and the program page states it before you apply. Who can apply? Anyone 18 or older who has not previously completed an LFX Mentorship program. Do I need to be a student? No. Some programs ask for school enrollment verification as a prerequisite, but many do not. The program page lists the prerequisites. How many programs can I apply to? You may have up to three applications open at a time. Withdrawing an application frees a slot. How much time does a term take? A significant weekly commitment across a multi-week term. Each program page lists its own term dates. How are applicants chosen? The program's mentors review each application against the skills the program lists and what you wrote in your cover letter, then accept for the term. What happens at the end of a term? You complete a final evaluation with your mentor. Graduating is recorded on your public mentee profile. Do I need an account to browse? No. Programs, mentees and mentors are all public. You need an LF ID to apply, to mentor, or to administer a program. Where do I actually apply? Applying happens in LFX, not on this site. Apply to This Program on a program page takes you to app.lfx.dev. See Apply to a Program. Related sections Getting Started Apply to a Program

title: Mentees
description: Become an LFX Mentorship mentee, apply to a program, and find mentees in the public directory.
content: A mentee is a contributor taking part in a program for one term. Mentees do scoped work from the project's backlog and review it with a named mentor. What you can do Create a mentee profile and apply to up to three programs at a time Track your applications and complete the tasks a program sets Browse the public mentee directory and read mentee profiles Eligibility You are 18 or older. You can commit consistent hours for the full term. You may have up to 3 open applications at a time. You may only complete one LFX Mentorship program in your career. Where things happen Browsing the mentee directory happens here. Everything else — your profile, your applications and your tasks — happens in LFX at app.lfx.dev/mentorship/mentee. In this section Become a Mentee — create your mentee profile Apply to a Program — submit an application Mentee Directory — browse and read mentee profiles Mentees FAQ Related sections Programs — find a program before you apply Mentors — the people who review your work

title: Apply to a Program
description: How to apply to an LFX Mentorship program, what the prerequisites are, and what happens next.
content: Applying happens in LFX. This site is where you find the program; the application itself is at app.lfx.dev. Before you begin You need a mentee profile. See Become a Mentee. You may have at most three open applications at a time. Withdrawing one frees a slot. Check the program's prerequisites on its page first — several ask for a resume, a cover letter on set topics, a coding challenge, or school enrollment verification. Check Applications close in the program sidebar. Steps 1. Open the program you want from Find a Program. 2. Select Apply to This Program. You are taken to LFX and asked to sign in. 3. Confirm you meet the program's eligibility checks. 4. Complete each prerequisite the program requires. 5. Acknowledge the program terms and the compliance confirmation. 6. Submit the application. After completing Your application appears in your mentee overview at app.lfx.dev/mentorship/mentee, and the program's mentors review it against the skills the program listed and what you wrote. Outcome | What it means | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------ | Pending | Submitted and waiting on mentor review | Accepted | You have a place on the term; your tasks appear in LFX | Declined | The program did not take you on for this term | A turned-down application is always declined. You can apply to a different program, or to the same program in a later term. Related Program Pages — check prerequisites and dates before applying Mentees FAQ Become a Mentee

title: Become a Mentee
description: How to create your LFX Mentorship mentee profile before applying to a program.
content: Your mentee profile is what program mentors read first. It has to exist before you can apply to anything. Before you begin You need an LF ID. Creating one is free. You must be 18 or older. Have your skills, links and a short introduction ready. Steps 1. Select My Mentorship in the top navigation, or go straight to app.lfx.dev/mentorship/mentee. 2. Sign in with your LF ID. 3. Fill in the mentee registration form. It asks for your introduction, your skills, and the links a mentor would want to see. 4. Save the profile. After completing Your profile is live and you can apply to programs. If you already had a profile, opening the same link takes you straight to your mentee overview instead of the form. Related Apply to a Program — the next step Mentee Directory — where your profile appears once you join a program Browsing Programs

title: Mentees FAQ
description: Common questions about mentee applications, withdrawals, tasks and graduation.
content: How many programs can I apply to at once? Three. Withdrawing an application frees a slot straight away. Can I apply to the same program twice? You can apply to a program again in a later term. You cannot have two open applications to the same term. How do I withdraw an application? In LFX, open your mentee overview at app.lfx.dev/mentorship/mentee and withdraw from the application. Withdrawing frees one of your three slots. My application says "declined" — can I reapply? Yes, to a different program or to a later term of the same one. Declined is the status for any application that is not taken on; it is not a ban. Where are my tasks? Under My Tasks in LFX at app.lfx.dev/mentorship/mentee. Tasks set before you are accepted are part of your application; tasks set after you are accepted are the term's work. Can I do a second mentorship? No. You may complete one LFX Mentorship program in your career. When do I get paid? Where a program is funded, the stipend is paid in milestone installments across the term, and the final installment follows the final evaluation. Amounts vary by program and by your country of residence. Why is my profile not in the mentee directory? The directory lists mentees who have joined a program. Creating a profile alone does not list you. Related sections Apply to a Program Getting Started FAQ

title: Mentee Directory
description: Browse LFX Mentorship mentees and read their public profiles.
content: The mentee directory is the public list of everyone taking part in, or graduated from, an LFX Mentorship program. Before you begin No sign-in is required. A mentee appears here once they join a program; a mentee profile alone does not list you. Steps 1. Select Mentees from the top navigation. 2. Filter the list: All, Active or Graduated All skills — show only mentees who list a given skill 3. Select a mentee to open their public profile. 4. The profile shows their introduction, their skills, their links, and the programs they have taken part in. Related Become a Mentee — how your own profile gets here Mentor Directory

title: Mentors
description: Become an LFX Mentorship mentor, respond to a program invitation, and find mentors in the public directory.
content: A mentor is an experienced project contributor who scopes a mentee's work, reviews what they submit, and scores applicants for the term. What you can do Create a mentor profile and ask to mentor a program Accept or decline an invitation from a Program Admin Review applications, set and review tasks, and leave notes on a mentee Browse the public mentor directory and read mentor profiles How you join a program Two routes, and both end with the Program Admin: Route | How it starts | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | Invitation | A Program Admin invites you by email. The link takes you to LFX, where you accept or decline. | Request | You ask to mentor a program from your My Programs page in LFX. The Program Admin approves or declines the request. | Where things happen Browsing the mentor directory happens here. Your profile, your programs and your reviews happen in LFX at app.lfx.dev/mentorship/mentor. In this section Become a Mentor — create your mentor profile Mentor Invitations — respond to an invitation from a Program Admin Mentor Directory — browse and read mentor profiles Mentors FAQ Related sections Enroll a Program — for Program Admins who need mentors Programs

title: Become a Mentor
description: How to create your LFX Mentorship mentor profile and ask to mentor a program.
content: A mentor profile is what Program Admins and applicants see. It has to exist before you can join a program. Before you begin You need an LF ID. Have your introduction, skills and project links ready — the same things a mentee reads before applying. Steps 1. Select Become a Mentor in the top navigation, or go to app.lfx.dev/mentorship/mentor. 2. Sign in with your LF ID. 3. Fill in the mentor registration form and save it. 4. To join a program, open My Programs in LFX and request the program you want to mentor. After completing The Program Admin approves or declines your request. You can withdraw a request while it is still open. Once you are on a program, its mentees and tasks appear under My Programs. If you already had a mentor profile, opening the same link takes you straight to My Programs rather than the form. Related Mentor Invitations — if a Program Admin invited you instead Mentor Directory

title: Mentors FAQ
description: Common questions about mentoring an LFX Mentorship program.
content: How do I get onto a program? Either a Program Admin invites you by email, or you request the program from My Programs in LFX and the Program Admin approves it. I was invited but the link does not work. Invitation links are one-time. Ask the Program Admin to send a fresh invitation. Can I withdraw a request to mentor? Yes, while the request is still open. Open My Programs in LFX and withdraw it. Can I mentor more than one program? Yes. Every program you mentor appears under My Programs. Where do I review what a mentee submitted? Open the program from My Programs in LFX, then the mentee's tasks. You review each submitted task there. How do I record something about a mentee? Leave a note on the mentee from the program's mentee list in LFX. Notes are for the program's mentors and Program Admins, not for the mentee. Why does the site say "Program Admin" and not "maintainer"? "Maintainer" means an upstream project maintainer elsewhere in LFX. The person who administers a mentorship program is a Program Admin. Related sections Become a Mentor Mentor Invitations

title: Mentor Directory
description: Browse LFX Mentorship mentors and read their public profiles.
content: The mentor directory is the public list of everyone mentoring on LFX Mentorship. Before you begin No sign-in is required. Steps 1. Select Mentors from the top navigation. 2. Use All skills to show only mentors who list a given skill. 3. Each card shows the mentor's name, how long they have been mentoring, their introduction and their skills. 4. Select View Profile to open the full profile. 5. The profile shows their introduction, skills, links, and the programs they mentor. Related Become a Mentor — how your own profile gets here Mentee Directory

title: Mentor Invitations
description: How to accept or decline an invitation to mentor an LFX Mentorship program.
content: A Program Admin can invite you to mentor their program by email. The invitation is answered in LFX, not in the email itself. Before you begin The invitation email contains a one-time link. Use the link rather than navigating by hand. You need an LF ID. If you do not have a mentor profile yet, you are asked to create one. Steps 1. Open the invitation email and select its link. It takes you to the invitation page in LFX. 2. Sign in with your LF ID if you are not already signed in. 3. Review the program named on the page. 4. Select Accept or Decline. Nothing is answered until you make that choice on the page, so a mail scanner that follows the link cannot accept or decline on your behalf. After completing Accepting puts the program under My Programs in LFX, where its mentees and tasks appear. Declining leaves the program unchanged and notifies the Program Admin. Related Become a Mentor Enroll a Program — the Program Admin's side of the same flow

title: Programs
description: Find open mentorship programs and read what a program expects before you apply.
content: A program is one project's mentorship offering. Every program belongs to a Linux Foundation project, lists the skills it is looking for, and runs in dated terms. What you can do Browse every program across all participating foundations Filter by status and by skill, and search by name Open a program to read its description, term dates, stipend, mentors, mentees and sponsors Start an application from the program page Program status Status | What it means | --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | Accepting | The term is open and taking applications | Opens soon | The term is announced but applications have not opened yet | In progress | The term is under way; applications are closed | Completed | The term has finished | Only approved programs appear on this site. A program that was not approved during moderation is rejected and is never listed. In this section Browsing Programs — search, filter and sort the program list Program Pages — what each tab on a program page tells you Related sections Apply to a Program — turn a program you like into an application Enroll a Program — offer a program for your own project

title: Browsing Programs
description: How to find and filter open mentorship programs on LFX Mentorship.
content: Find a Program lists every program across all participating foundations, including terms already under way. Before you begin No sign-in is required to browse programs. To apply to one you will need an LF ID account. Steps 1. Select Find a Program from the top navigation. 2. Each card shows the project logo, the term, the program name, a short description, the skills the program lists, and how many mentors it has. 3. Narrow the list: Search — type part of a program or project name. Status pills — All, Accepting, In progress or Completed. All skills — pick a skill to show only programs that list it. Accepting First — change the sort order. 4. Select View program on any card to open the program page. After completing The program page opens, with its term dates, stipend, mentors and mentees. See Program Pages. Related Program Pages — reading a program page Apply to a Program — apply once you have found one

title: Program Pages
description: What each part of an LFX Mentorship program page tells you before you apply.
content: A program page is where you decide whether a program is a fit. It carries the term dates, the stipend, the skills, and the people already involved. Before you begin No sign-in is required to read a program page. Steps 1. Open any program from Find a Program. 2. Read the header. It carries the project logo and name, the program's status badge, and the skills the program lists. 3. Check the sidebar for the facts that decide whether you can take part: Field | What it tells you | ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | Term | Which term this page is for | Applications close | The last day to apply | Stipend | The amount, or that the amount is determined by mentee location | 4. Open Overview for the program description and what the project expects from a mentee. 5. Open Terms for the dates of this and any earlier terms. Applications are always made to a term, so check which one is open before you apply. 6. Open Mentors to see who will review your work. 7. Open Mentees for the program's current mentees and the ones who have graduated from earlier terms, each with the term they took part in. 8. Open Sponsors to see who funds the program, where it is funded. 9. Use the header actions: Apply to This Program — opens the application in LFX. Repository — the project's source repository. Donate — fund the program through LFX Crowdfunding. Code of Conduct — the project's code of conduct. After completing Apply to This Program takes you to app.lfx.dev, where the application itself lives. See Apply to a Program. Related Browsing Programs Apply to a Program Enroll a Program — if you want to run a program like this one
